title: Install Ollama
task: Install Ollama on your machine and confirm the command works. macOS and Windows: download the installer from ollama.com (Ollama for Windows ships as preview builds; grab the current one). Linux: run the one-line install script shown on the same page.

checks.prompt: Does `ollama --version` print a version number (and not "command not found")?

hints.text: If the command is not found after installing, the Ollama app may not be running yet. Start it, open a fresh terminal, and try again.
Windows: after the installer finishes, Ollama usually starts itself in the system tray; open a new PowerShell or terminal window for the command.

solution: Install from https://ollama.com for your platform, then run `ollama --version` in a new terminal window.

title: Pull a small model
task: Download a small model and see it in your local library. llama3.2:1b is the 1-billion-parameter model and the download is about 1-2 GB, so check your disk space and your data plan before pulling. Later labs in this pack reuse it.

checks.prompt: Does `ollama list` show llama3.2:1b with a size of roughly 1-2 GB?

hints.text: The tag matters: llama3.2:1b is the small one. Tags like llama3.2:70b are much larger downloads.
Watch the progress bar. The weights land in Ollama's model folder on your own disk.

title: Chat with your model
task: Start a chat with the model in your terminal, ask it two questions, then leave the chat cleanly.

checks.prompt: Did the model answer both questions in the terminal?
Did `/bye` return you to your normal shell prompt?

hints.text: Type your question and press Enter. The first reply can pause for a few seconds while the model loads into memory.
Leave the chat with `/bye` (or Ctrl+D), not by closing the terminal.

solution: ollama run llama3.2:1b, ask your questions, then /bye

title: Feel the temperature dial
task: Ask the same question twice at low temperature and twice at high temperature, then compare how much the answers move.
commands: Give me one unusual name for a coffee shop.
Give me one unusual name for a coffee shop.

checks.prompt: At temperature 0.1, were repeated answers similar to each other?
At temperature 1.5, did the answers wander further apart?

hints.text: Inside the chat, run `/set parameter temperature 0.1`, ask the question, then `/set parameter temperature 1.5` and ask again.
Prefer the REST route? POST to http://localhost:11434/api/generate with {"model": "llama3.2:1b", "prompt": "...", "stream": false, "options": {"temperature": 1.5}} in the JSON body.

solution: ollama run llama3.2:1b, then /set parameter temperature 0.1, ask twice, then /set parameter temperature 1.5, ask twice, then /bye

title: Watch the model forget you
task: Prove the model keeps nothing between sessions: tell it your name in one chat, leave, start a fresh chat, and ask for your name again.

checks.prompt: Within the first session, did the model use your name correctly later in that same session?
In the second session, did the model fail to know your name?

hints.text: Two separate `ollama run` sessions are two separate conversations.
Within one session the app resends the transcript, so the name appears remembered. Between sessions there is no transcript to resend.

solution: ollama run llama3.2:1b, say "My name is <your name>", /bye, then ollama run llama3.2:1b again and ask "What is my name?"

title: Catch a confident invention
task: Ask the model about the borrowing rules of a small club that does not exist, press for exact figures, then ask again in a fresh session and compare the inventions.
commands: ollama run llama3.2:1b "According to the Harbour Street Book Club borrowing rules, how many books can a member borrow at once, and what is the fine per week for a late return?"
ollama run llama3.2:1b "According to the Harbour Street Book Club borrowing rules, how many books can a member borrow at once, and what is the fine per week for a late return?"

checks.prompt: Did the model produce specific numbers for a club that does not exist?
Comparing the two runs, did the invented numbers stay the same?

hints.text: If the model hedges, follow up the way an impatient user would: "just give me the numbers".
Specific figures with no source are the tell. The confidence in the tone is borrowed from questions it can usually answer.

solution: ollama run llama3.2:1b "According to the Harbour Street Book Club borrowing rules, how many books can a member borrow at once, and what is the fine per week for a late return?" (run twice and compare)

title: Prove it stays home
task: Turn off Wi-Fi (or unplug the network cable), ask the local model a question, get an answer, then turn the network back on. The answer arriving with every path out of the machine closed is proof that no prompt was transmitted.
commands: ollama run llama3.2:1b "In one sentence, what is a cairn?"

checks.prompt: With Wi-Fi off, did the model still answer?
Does `ollama ps` show the model running against localhost?

hints.text: Turn the network off before running the command, and turn it back on afterwards.
No policy document can add anything to this demonstration, because the event the policies govern did not occur.

solution: Wi-Fi off, then ollama run llama3.2:1b "In one sentence, what is a cairn?", then Wi-Fi back on
